study: Benchmark-suite study, design of November 2026 (SafetyPointGoal1-v0). Runner: safety_study_v76.py. Design note of 16 November 2026. The stored runs of safety_pilot_v63.py and safety_ramp_v65.py are not touched.

smoke.note: Short runs that test the runner; no result of the study.

pilot-no-price.note: Pilot, first part (16 November 2026). No price, from scratch, two seeds, 16 million steps, constant against linearly decayed learning rate. Questions: when the run levels off, what the controller without a price reaches, and which of the two learning-rate settings the study uses. The learner's settings are chosen on this stage alone.

pilot-price.note: Pilot, second part. Each run continues for 6 million steps from the controller without a price of its seed, taken from the constant-rate run of the first part at 10 million steps (the stored copy, which is the policy evaluated at that step), with that controller's observation normalization kept fixed and a constant learning rate. Prices 0.04, 0.08 and 0.16 imposed at once, and the run without a price continued equally. Questions: the direction and size of the change, whether each policy scores at least as well at its own price as the controller without a price and as never moving, when the runs level off, and how far the parameters travel from the controller (the scale of the anchor).

pilot-anchor.note: Pilot, third part. The runs of the second part at the price 0.08, repeated with the anchor toward the controller they start from, at three constant strengths a factor of ten apart. The scale comes from the first seed of the second part: without an anchor the parameters end about 13 from the controller at every price, the price 0 included, and the norm of the mean gradient of a rollout is about 0.012, so that the pull equals that norm at that distance for a strength near 0.001; the strengths 0.01 and 0.1 would hold the parameters near 1.2 and 0.12 by the same rule. Questions: where each strength holds the parameters, and what it does to the stopped utility, which fell from 10.6 to about 7 in the unanchored run at this price, and to the exhaustion probability.

pilot-diagnosis.note: Pilot, diagnosis (17 November 2026). Not a part of the design. In the second part the policies trained under a price did not beat the controller they started from at that price, and at 0.16 they stayed below never moving, although a rule made by hand on the same controller (stop once 40 % of the budget is used, script safety_stop_rule_v76.py) scores well above the trained policy on both seeds (3.1 and -0.3 against about -10 and -12) and on the first seed above never moving, and the critic had taken up the charge (script safety_reserve_response_v76.py). This stage repeats the run at the price 0.16 with one setting of the learner changed at a time, to see which of them lets the policy follow the charge: minibatches eight times larger, an entropy bonus, the action dispersion of the controller set back to 0.5 (it had narrowed to about 0.19), and a learning rate ten times smaller. The comparison is the run price-0.16 of the second part.
